name: Gum lift

lead: A gum lift reshapes the gumline to expose more of the tooth, rebalancing a gummy smile or short-looking teeth. It overlaps with crown lengthening, a procedure done by periodontists.

Gum tissue is removed and sometimes supporting bone is reshaped to a lower level, with the flap repositioned. Braces to extrude the tooth are an alternative. No registered trials directly study cosmetic gum lifts; sources describe the technique and its trade-offs.

paras: A periodontist performs it, with the change visible after healing. Soreness typically lasts one to two weeks. Cosmetic dentistry sources describe gum contouring as making teeth look longer or more even.
Bone removal is irreversible and can weaken neighbouring support and complicate implants. The gum margin may drift back toward the crown over time.

angle.text: Users with a gummy smile or short-looking teeth have the gumline reshaped to show more tooth, overlapping with crown lengthening. The change shows once the gums heal, and research specific to cosmetic use is limited.

lead: A gum lift is the cosmetic term for reshaping the gumline to expose more of the tooth, a procedure that overlaps with crown lengthening [1][2]. Crown lengthening is a surgical procedure, usually performed by a periodontist, that exposes more tooth by removing some gum tissue and sometimes supporting bone [1].

It has functional uses, such as improving retention for a crown or reaching decay below the gumline, and aesthetic uses such as adjusting gum-to-tooth proportions in a gummy smile [1]. Cosmetic dentistry sources describe gum contouring as making teeth look longer or more even [2]. Wikipedia's crown lengthening article does not use the term gum lift [1].

Bone removal is irreversible, and the gum margin may gradually shift back toward the crown after surgery [1]. No trial in the registered set examined cosmetic gum lifts directly; registered gum-surgery trials concern recession coverage.
infobox: Apically repositioned flap with bone reshaping; orthodontic extrusion
Irreversible bone removal, gum margin may drift back

paras: The flap approach lifts the gum, reshapes bone at a more apical level and repositions the flap; it suits several teeth in one area rather than a single front tooth [1]. Forced eruption instead uses braces to move the tooth into position, preserving neighbouring bone but needing fixed appliances and more time [1].
The procedure is used to alter gum and tooth proportions in a gummy smile [1]. Gum contouring is listed among cosmetic gum procedures alongside gum grafts and gingivectomy [2].
Functional indications include improving crown retention and resistance, accessing decay below the gumline, perforations and external root resorption [1].

Removing bone weakens support for neighbouring teeth, worsens the crown-to-root ratio, and lost bone is described as almost impossible to restore, which may limit later implant options [1]. Flap surgery causes more postoperative pain for some patients, and restorations that encroach on the attachment tissue can lead to chronic inflammation, recession and bone loss [1]. Soreness usually resolves in one to two weeks [1].

No studies found for cosmetic gum lifts in the registered set. Related registered trials concern recession treatment, such as a coronally advanced tunnel technique with a collagen matrix in 36 participants (completed) and a comparison of a modified tunnel technique with a flap for Class III recessions (completed) [3][4]. A pilot study mentioned on Wikipedia found that starting prosthetic work at six weeks gave results comparable to 14 weeks after crown lengthening [1].
